title: Foundation I — The Body That Sits
tradition: Sōtō Zen foundation with a personal pre-zazen kuji threshold
description: A first-week daily form that preserves your nine-seal threshold, uses brief susokukan as scaffolding, and places the center of gravity in uncontrived shikantaza.
weeklyTeaching: Practice and realization are not two.
weeklyTeachingNote: Do not grade the sitting by tranquility, silence, or attainment. Wholehearted return to sitting is the practice.

stages.title: Kuji threshold
stages.instruction: Begin in gasshō. Move through the nine seals without attaching invented powers or meanings. This is your threshold; zazen begins after it.
stages.secondary: Two quiet breaths per seal is sufficient. Keep the seals precise, unhurried, and simple.

stages.title: Settle the body
stages.instruction: Return to gasshō and bow. Set the hokkaijōin. Upright spine, chin slightly tucked, shoulders released, eyes open and naturally lowered.
stages.secondary: Take one full exhalation. Sway gently left and right, decreasing the movement until the body comes to rest in the center. Then stop adjusting.

cues.text: Let the mouth close naturally; tongue lightly to the roof of the mouth. Breathe through the nose.
Come to center. Nothing further needs to be arranged.

stages.title: Susokukan
stages.instruction: Let breathing be natural. At each completed exhalation, count silently from one to ten, then return to one.
stages.secondary: Do not engineer a ratio, squeeze the abdomen, or target a breathing rate. If the count is lost or runs past ten, simply return to one. Nothing went wrong.

cues.text: Feel the body breathing rather than manufacturing the breath.
When distraction is recognized, return without commentary: one.

stages.title: Shikantaza
stages.instruction: Release the count. Do not expand awareness, narrow it, chase silence, observe yourself observing, or try to produce mushin. Just remain sitting.
stages.secondary: Thoughts may arise. Do not complete them and do not attack them. When you discover that thought has closed around you, open the hand of thought and return to the whole body sitting upright.

cues.text: Nothing special is required. Sit upright; let phenomena come and go.
Do not ask whether shikantaza is happening. Return to sitting.

stages.title: Leave slowly
stages.instruction: At the bell, bring the hands to gasshō and bow. Place the hands on the thighs. Take one fuller breath.
stages.secondary: Sway gently, beginning small and becoming larger. Unfold the legs carefully and rise deliberately. Do not rush the transition.

cues.text: If there is sharp pain or persistent numbness, move carefully. Zen does not require injuring the body.

inquiries: What was I trying to get from that sitting?
What would the sitting have been if nothing whatsoever had been obtained?

study.contemplation: What does it mean to study the self? Notice the recurring division between ‘me’ and ‘what is happening to me’ during ordinary life; do not turn this into an exercise during zazen.
